name: stats-836e5219-blind30-ots
instr:
# Repairing a batch of silent numeric faults in montanaflynn/stats without a test suite

I use this Go library to boil batches of measurements down to single figures and to compare one batch of readings against another. After upgrading to the current checkout, a great many calls give me answers I cannot reconcile with what they used to return, or with arithmetic I can do by hand, and elsewhere calls fail that used to work or stay quiet where they used to object. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Below is everything I was able to pin down from the outside, described by what I asked for and what came back.

Condensing a single list into one figure goes wrong in several ways. Asking which value or values occur most often no longer returns the set that actually repeats most often; an eight-number list whose only repeated value is 5 does not report 5 on its own, and several other lists come back with a set that is simply not what repeats. The reciprocal-based average of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 should round to 2.19 and instead comes back many times too large, the error growing as the list gets longer, although lists holding a zero or a negative are refused as before. The uncertainty figure for a list containing a zero entry now evaluates to not-a-number, while lists whose entries are all strictly positive still give what I expect. Multiplying every value together fails at both edges: a one-element list such as a lone 7 comes back with a complaint and a not-a-number
